name: movement disorders overview
title: Tremor or slowness: a symmetric postural or action tremor that improves with alcohol is essential tremor; asymmetric rest tremor with rigidity, bradykinesia and postural instability is parkinsonism, which is Parkinson's disease only once drugs, basal ganglia lesions, head trauma, toxins, PSP and MSA are excluded; each with its treatment and the lecture's video cases

root.title: Tremor or slowness: WHEN is the tremor worst, and is it on ONE side?
lines: • hyperkinetic (too much movement): ballismus · chorea · athetosis · tremor · dystonia · tics
• hypokinetic (too little): parkinsonism, with bradykinesia (slow) and akinesia (hard to start)
• rest + ASYMMETRIC + slow + small writing → parkinsonism · posture or action + SYMMETRIC + large writing → essential tremor
• parkinsonism needs NO treatment until symptoms limit function

groups.title: PARKINSONISM: a syndrome
lines: tremor · rigidity · bradykinesia · postural instability, in any mix

head: h
Essential tremor
may be hereditary · worsens over time
pres: • arms most, also head and voice
now spills food and drink · no other illness → reassure: NOT Parkinson's · beta-blocker after discussing side effects

head: h
Parkinson's disease
dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra die
1% of people over 60 · onset about 60
mostly sporadic, rarely hereditary
pres: • Tremor at REST early, pill-rolling, hands or feet
• Rigidity: same at any speed (spasticity is velocity dependent), ↑ with augmentation
• Akinesia: rising from a chair, starting to walk
• Bradykinesia: finger or foot tapping, fist open-close, turning a doorknob
• less blinking · masked face · soft, mumbling voice
• rigid, NOT spastic tone · small handwriting
• less arm swing · stooped, turns en bloc
• 74, no medications, told 'maybe PD' → agree, start LEVODOPA
• 60, 1 year subtle left tremor, slowness, mild rigidity → early PD, NO treatment yet
• 10 years of PD, gait worsens → medication WORE OFF
tx: Not functionally limiting → no treatment yet
• dopamine cannot cross the blood-brain barrier; levodopa CAN
• with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor: carbidopa (Sinemet) or benserazide (Prolopa)
• most effective: bradykinesia, rigidity best · tremor variable
• start low, titrate slowly · NEVER stop suddenly (sudden worsening)
• watch: on-off, wearing off · dyskinesia, chorea or dystonia (50% by 5 years)
slowly worsens · dyskinesia · depression · dementia · death usually from ASPIRATION pneumonia

head: h
Parkinsonism from ANOTHER cause
Parkinson's disease is only ONE cause
pres: • basal ganglia stroke, bleed, tumour, infection
• repeated head trauma · carbon monoxide, cyanide
• VERTICAL gaze palsy: pursuit and saccades overcome by vestibular reflexes
tx: Do NOT call it Parkinson's disease
• other neurodegenerative causes: MSA, PSP, diffuse Lewy body disease
• MSA: death within 6-9 years of onset
